first_impression.reaction: My assistant put this on the list because the family hasn't settled where the legal marriage happens, and if it's abroad, the Sydney side of the family will ask about names and passports. The first screen is calm and factual, with no gushing. Honestly, I'll probably keep my own name, as most women in my family do, so most of this is for my assistant. Her summary for me: married abroad means no automatic name change in NSW or Victoria, so bring home the foreign certificate, translated and legalised, and book travel in the name on the passport. I read the intro, the passport section and the overseas section myself. She took the step list and the states.

journey.quote: Marry overseas and the picture shifts.
journey.reaction: Good. It tells me in the second paragraph that the part that applies to us is covered, so my assistant knew where to point me.

journey.quote: Keeping your name asks nothing of you.
journey.reaction: That's my most likely choice, and it's nice not to be made to feel I'm opting out. Short and respectful.

journey.section: Step 1: Get the official registry marriage certificate (not the ceremonial one)
journey.quote: The handsome certificate you sign at the ceremony is a keepsake.
journey.reaction: Useful and said gracefully. My assistant will make sure whoever handles the paperwork orders the real one.

journey.section: Step 6: Work, professional registrations and everything else
journey.quote: For NSW residents it also names the NSW Land Registry if you own a home, the Rental Bond Board if you rent, and the NSW Pet Registry if you have a pet.
journey.reaction: Rental bonds and pet registries. This is clearly written for someone else. My assistant skipped it; it's the moment the page stopped feeling like it was for me.

journey.section: Changing your name on your passport after marriage
journey.quote: It recommends booking travel in the name that's in your passport.
journey.reaction: This is the line our office actually needs. Family members flying from Dubai, Sydney and London, and tickets booked by different people. Clear and practical.

journey.section: State by state: NSW, Victoria, Queensland and Western Australia
journey.quote: As at November 2026, the registries agree on the broad shape but word the details differently.
journey.reaction: Fair, but then it's four states and a paragraph on the rest. Thorough for a reference page; for me it's my assistant's job, not mine.

journey.section: Name change after an overseas or destination wedding
journey.quote: Smartraveller says a foreign marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of the marriage, but you may be unable to use it as proof of a name change.
journey.reaction: This is the one thing I didn't know, and it's the reason this page earned its place on the shortlist. If we marry legally abroad, the Australian side has extra paperwork.

journey.section: Name change after an overseas or destination wedding
journey.quote: Foreign certificates it accepts must also be legalised, so check [whether your certificate needs an apostille](https://weddedwonderland.com/expert-advice/what-is-an-apostille-and-does-my-paperwork-need-one) well ahead of the wedding.
journey.reaction: Good. A concrete task with a lead time, the kind of thing a family office wants flagged early.

journey.section: Name change after an overseas or destination wedding
journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor, start to finish, plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments as your single point of contact; the name change and every certificate stay with you and the official agencies.
journey.reaction: Honest about where their role ends, which I respect. But one advisor for 300 guests across three countries? Nothing about scale, exclusive use or discretion. I'd want to know who sits behind that one person.

journey.quote: Once you know which certificate you will come home with, the rest is the part your guests remember.
journey.reaction: Warm without being eager. A good line to close on.

journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, anywhere in the world, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: 'Anywhere in the world' suits us. Leading with the fee being agreed upfront reads as reassurance for someone worried about being overcharged. That isn't my concern.

unanswered_questions: Have they planned a celebration abroad for 200 to 400 guests, with exclusive use and our own security working with the venue's?
Does one Wedded Advisor work alone, or is there a team behind them at our scale?
How are our personal documents and details handled if we share certificates or passport names with them for travel bookings?
Is there a private or referral route to someone senior, rather than the Wedded Concierge web page?
Can they coordinate guest travel for family flying in from Dubai, Sydney and London at once?

turn_offs_found.quote: For NSW residents it also names the NSW Land Registry if you own a home, the Rental Bond Board if you rent, and the NSW Pet Registry if you have a pet.
turn_offs_found.why: Over-explaining for a reader like me, and rental bonds and pet registries signal the page is pitched at a standard client. It's the point where the brand stops feeling like it's speaking to my family.

turn_offs_found.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, anywhere in the world, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins.
turn_offs_found.why: Putting the fee up front reads as value reassurance, the language of a budget-conscious client. I don't want 'no surprises'. I want to know what's possible.

would_share_with: My assistant and family office, for the passport booking line and the overseas certificate, translation and apostille steps
My Sydney cousins, if the legal marriage ends up abroad and they ask what it means for names

cta_reaction.why: The tone is quiet and they're clear they don't handle the legal side, which I respect. But nothing speaks to scale or discretion, and the close is pitched at a couple worried about fees. I wouldn't fill in a web form. With a referral from someone we trust, my assistant would make the call.

top_3_changes: In the Wedded Advisor paragraph under 'Name change after an overseas or destination wedding' or in 'Planning the celebration', add one line inviting couples with large guest lists, families across several countries or privacy needs to say so when they first get in touch. It acknowledges scale and discretion without claiming capabilities the page can't support.
In 'Keeping your name', add a short, neutral line noting that in many families and cultures keeping your own family name is simply the norm. It shows cultural awareness without stereotyping anyone.

In 'Planning the celebration', lead with 'anywhere in the world' and move 'with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins' out of the lead sentence, so the close reads as what's possible rather than as reassurance on cost.
